summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with embedded controls and firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4 and Arduino platforms. Built bare-metal C/C++ firmware with timer-triggered ADC sampling, interrupt-driven I2C/UART drivers, and FreeRTOS task coordination for real-time sensing and motor control. Hands-on with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers for embedded hardware debugging and validation.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF motion into real-time HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in embedded C with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture, achieving deterministic 1 Hz real-time sensing.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); wrote low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across sensing, control, and display tasks; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection for closed-loop grasping.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
